title: Seamless Blocking
content:
I have tested the new Seamless Blocking feature.

I would like to use it to create a subsection defined by a complex curve in the interior of the parent shape that is overlapped with another shape underneath--the shape that is curved. 

Unlike internal lines and pattern outlines, I cannot use the Copy/Replace line option to exactly replicate the complex curve, nor can I select that exact shape line and offset as a Seamless Blocking line (if offset is zero) nor can I convert an internal line to a Seamless Blocking line to retain that complex curve. 

I can imperfectly replicate the curve in a few ways but this manual and inexact workaround is not efficient. 

If you have some insight into how I may accomplish this, please share. Thank you, friends!

P.S. One of my pattern piece perimeters was not the same in Print Layout. There is a glitch with that for sure.

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Hi there, would it be possible to share screenshots of your CLO window with the pattern pieces visible? Maybe the curved shape is not intersecting with the pattern outline which would result in it not working.

title: One question from beginner
content:
How can i reapair collision when I make men`s suit with a shirt and vest at the sleeves?

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: This is with deleted shirt sleeve. Particle distance 5, tried even with 1 same result.
Reply 1: (Hi there, sorry for not seeing this earlier, if a reply is not directly under my own comment, there is no notification sent to me.) Since you deleted the shirt sleeves here, I cannot make out where the collision happened, however it is preferable to layer such complex garments on a standard pose, and especially when it comes to suits - because of their reduced mobility in the armpit area - in the pose "A_Narrow". This will lower the margins for error when layering. How did you layer? Did you use the Layer setting in the PE? If small parts are still colliding, you can fix them with one of the Select Mesh tools: https://connect.clo-set.com/community/post/4a2c3bc1f11b4f2f8f17d1921b52c51e
Reply 2: Thank you, i will try.

Comment 2: Hi, please share a screenshot so we can assess possible next steps.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on how to fix collisions or fitting issues when tailoring men's suits with shirts and vests at the sleeves.

I am interested in how the site ensures that the creators' models and designs are protected from being sold or transferred to people who did not purchase the product.

I would also like to know if it is possible to add watermarks or trademarks to your models and designs for additional protection. 

I also have a question about the basic and extended license when purchasing a product, does the site guarantee that the person who bought my design or model will not use them for commercial purposes, like how does the site guarantee this?? Anyone can buy my product with a basic license (for example, a T-shirt for 2 dollar) and use it for commercial purposes, for example, in their commercial videos or 3D works in other applications or sites, and what should I do with this??

Hello, CLO friends!

CLO 2025.1 is now available, featuring 28 new functions developed based on user feedback.

**✅ CLO 2025.1 Highlight Features:**

  * **Upgraded 3D Pen:** Draw garment silhouettes around the avatar directly from the 3D space, and instantly convert them into 2D patterns.

  * **Seamless Blocking:** Design seamless styles by applying different fabrics within a single pattern without any sewing lines.

  * **Denim Wet Wash Effect:** Easily apply various denim washes such as stone, enzyme, and bleach.

  * **Zipper Style:** Manage identical zipper styles as a single item for faster and more efficient workflow.

Check out [_other major features for the new version_](https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/features) and [_download the latest CLO_](https://www.clo3d.com/en/clo/download).

title: Standard Female US ASTM Sizes Missing
content:
I can't find the Standard Female US ASTM sizes in the new library window. There are all the files for EU, Missy, Maternity, Petite, Plus and Teen, but no Standard. Anyone else having this issue?![1ac9e45df2e24d5b8bd2012999982be2](https://storagefiles.clo-set.com/public/community/202508/fc21b3ae4f7a4df8bb35f0c473d9da62/images/1ac9e45df2e24d5b8bd2012999982be2Screenshot%202025-08-18%20at%2021.07.43.png)

### Community Post Comments:
Comment 1: Ah, okay, so Missy is the regular women's fit, versus Petite and Plus?

Comment 2: Hi, thanks for responding, yes, that is a screenshot of what I'm seeing in my library. There is Missy Curvy or Straight, Petite Curvy or Straight and Plus Curvy or Straight, but no Standard Curvy or Straight. Whereas Mens and Kids have all the sizes in the Standard range. Do you see what I mean?
Reply 1: Missy Curvy and Missy straight are the two standard versions, they just do not have the word standard. Mens has less variation/shaping in their sizes which is why there is just a folder labeled Standard. and there is no Standard size file for kids. Kids is sorted by ages 6 months to 12 years and then Boys and Girls

Comment 3: Hi There. Is that screenshot from your CLO? If so then you already have all the included ASTM female sizes. There is no regular size, but just choosing between curvy or straight
content_description: To provide users with support and solutions for locating Standard Female US ASTM size files in the new library window.
